# 2. Data Audit

#### Checking for missing values

```{r}
colSums(is.na(hotels_raw))
```

The vairables with missing data are:

- children - 4

- meal - 1169

- country - 488

- market_segment - 2

- distribution channel - 5

- agent - 16340

- company - 112593

## Dropping leakage variables

reservation_status and reservation_status_date give the outcome (we just need the var is_canceled). assigned_room_type and booking_changes are updated after the booking is made.

```{r}
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    select(-c(reservation_status, reservation_status_date, assigned_room_type, booking_changes))
```

## Changing data types

```{r}
str(hotels_raw)

# Data documentation tells us "Undefined" = "SC"
table(hotels_raw$meal) # "Undefined" level
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(meal = replace(meal, meal == "Undefined", "SC"),
           meal = factor(meal, levels = c("SC", "BB", "HB", "FB"), ordered = TRUE))

mean(is.na(hotels_raw$company)) # percent of company variable missing (94.3%)
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(has_company = ifelse(is.na(company), 0, 1)) 
        

hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(across(c(hotel, is_canceled, country, market_segment, distribution_channel,
                    is_repeated_guest, reserved_room_type, deposit_type, agent,
                    customer_type, has_company), as.factor),
           arrival_date_month = factor(arrival_date_month, levels = month.name, ordered = TRUE))

# Confirm
str(hotels_raw)
```

**Ordinal:** arrival_date_month, meal (SC \< BB \< HB \< FB)

**Nominal:** hotel, country, market_segment, distribution_channel, reserved_room_type, deposit_type, agent, customer_type

**Binary:** is_canceled (target), is_repeated_guest, has_company

## Modifying other data problems / Engineering new features

```{r}
hotels_raw |> skim()
```

```{r}
# Problems found in the raw data 
table(hotels_raw$market_segment) # "Undefined" level
table(hotels_raw$distribution_channel) # "Undefined" level
summary(hotels_raw$adr) # negative min, extreme max
mean(is.na(hotels_raw$company)) # percent of company variable missing (94.3%)
sum(hotels_raw$adults + hotels_raw$children + hotels_raw$babies == 0, na.rm = TRUE) # 180 zero-guest bookings
```

```{r}
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |>
    mutate(market_segment = replace(market_segment, market_segment == "Undefined", NA),
           distribution_channel = replace(distribution_channel, distribution_channel == "Undefined", NA),
           adr = replace(adr, adr < 0 | adr > 1000, NA),      # ASSUMPTION: impossible / extreme nightly rates
           agent = replace_na(as.character(agent), "None"),   # ASSUMPTION: no agent = booked directly
           total_nights = stays_in_weekend_nights + stays_in_week_nights,
           total_guests = adults + coalesce(children, 0) + babies) |>
    select(-company) # 94.3% of this variable is missing

# ASSUMPTION: bookings with zero guests are data errors
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |> filter(total_guests > 0)

# Drop unused levels 
hotels_raw <- hotels_raw |> droplevels()
```

## Data Exploration (univariate)

#### Target

```{r}
table(hotels_raw$is_canceled)
prop.table(table(hotels_raw$is_canceled))
```

#### Summary stats

```{r}
hotels_raw |> select_if(is.numeric) |> basicStats()
hotels_raw |> select_if(is.numeric) |> skewness(na.rm = TRUE)
```

#### Missing values

```{r}
missprop <- hotels_raw |> summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)) / length(.)))
print(missprop, width = Inf)
```

None of the variables that have missing data are missing THAT much of their data, which will hopefully make imputation easier and more reliable (we previously removed company with \~94.3% of its observations missing)

#### Numeric plots

```{r, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 3}
num_vars <- hotels_raw |> select(where(is.numeric)) |> names()

for (v in num_vars) {
    p <- ggplot(hotels_raw, aes(.data[[v]])) +
        geom_histogram(bins = 50) +
        ggtitle(v)
    print(p)
}
```

```{r}

sum(hotels_raw$total_guests > 10, na.rm = TRUE)

```

#### Categorical plots

```{r, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 3}
cat_vars <- hotels_raw |> select(where(is.factor)) |> names()

# Country and agent have hundreds of levels, so their charts are unreadable
# Skipping them in the loop and using a table instead
cat_vars <- setdiff(cat_vars, c("country", "agent"))
hotels_raw |> count(country, sort = TRUE) |> head(15)
hotels_raw |> count(agent, sort = TRUE) |> head(15)

for (v in cat_vars) {
    p <- ggplot(hotels_raw, aes(reorder(.data[[v]], .data[[v]], function(x) -length(x)))) +
        geom_bar() +
        xlab(v) +
        geom_text(aes(label = after_stat(count)), stat = "count", vjust = -0.3, size = 2) +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
    print(p)
}
```

## Data Exploration (bivariate)

#### Graphics

```{r}
num_vars <- hotels_raw |> select(where(is.numeric)) |> names()
cat_vars <- hotels_raw |> select(where(is.factor)) |> names()
cat_vars <- setdiff(cat_vars, c("is_canceled", "country", "agent"))  # drop target + too many levels
```

#### Numeric plots

```{r, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 3}
}
```
